thread:
jamie-support: Hey team — customer reports hosted model API works for quick inference but streaming sessions to Redwood Private in their VPC keep dropping after ~10–30s. They see lots of token gaps and client-side `connection reset`.
lina-sre: Which customer and region? Any error ids?
jamie-support: customer: AcmeHealth (private deployment in us-west-2). No error id in our side, their app logs show `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection was reset by peer` and our conn tracker on the private node shows `RST` after a few KB of the stream.
dustin-cust: Confirming — we can do short queries fine (<1s). Long-poll streaming (server->client) consistently drops around 15s. Happens across multiple client IPs.
deploy-bot: deployment/infra event: nginx-proxy v1.8 rolled 2026-02-25 03:12UTC to that cluster (no known changes to SG/NACL)
jamie-support: Collected tcpdump from customer side (NAT + private subnet). Key snippet below (S=server, C=client NAT):

```
20:12:01.123456 IP S.svc443 > NAT.56012: Flags [S.], seq 100, ack 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
20:12:01.123486 IP NAT.56012 > S.svc443: Flags [.], ack 101, win 502, length 0
20:12:15.678901 IP S.svc443 > NAT.56012: Flags [P.], seq 101:892, ack 1, win 64240, length 791
20:12:15.678915 IP NAT.56012 > S.svc443: Flags [R], seq 1, ack 0, win 0, length 0
```

jamie-support: Looks like server pushes data then a RST from NAT side. That typically indicates a misconfigured stateless NACL denying one direction of ephemeral ports.
networking-jen: Agreed. On AWS the NACLs are stateless — you need explicit allow for return port ranges. What do the customer's NACL rules look like?
jamie-support: They sent this Terraform module excerpt (sanitized):

```
acl_rule { cidr = "0.0.0.0/0" protocol = "tcp" rule_no = 100 action = "allow" port_range = "443-443" egress = true }
acl_rule { cidr = "0.0.0.0/0" protocol = "tcp" rule_no = 110 action = "deny" port_range = "32768-65535" egress = true }
```

lina-sre: Oof. They explicitly deny high ephemeral egress ports. If NAT translates client source to ephemeral ports in that range and the NACL denies egress, TCP will RST when server tries to push back or when new segments arrive. Also NACL deny order matters.
dustin-cust: Wait we only allowed 443 egress because of hardening guidance. Why would return traffic use high ports for egress? I thought client source port is ephemeral but egress rule is checked against source port on outbound from subnet.
networking-jen: Right — for egress checks on the NACL the source port is the ephemeral port on the host. If you deny ephemeral ports outbound, the NAT/host can't establish stateful flows. With TCP the initial SYN might succeed if using a low source port, but server pushes chunks and subsequent segments use ephemeral pairings and then get dropped or cause resets. Also some client libraries open additional parallel connections from different ephemeral ports for streaming multiplexing.
jamie-support: Repro steps we used to validate:
1) From private node `curl -v --no-buffer https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream ...` -> short queries OK, streaming fails with `Recv failure: Connection was reset`.
2) `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 tcp and host <model-host>` to capture RST pattern.
3) Temporarily updated NACL rule to allow `32768-65535` egress -> streaming stabilized, no RSTs observed.
lina-sre: Good repro. Also checked customer DNS and TLS — DNS resolves fine, TLS handshake completes (we see `SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK` and `ClientHello/ServerHello`), so it's not SNI or cert.
networking-jen: Suggested permanent fixes:
- Allow ephemeral port range (recommend AWS default 32768-65535) in both egress and ingress rules on the NACLs that cover the private subnets behind NAT.
- Or simplify by relying on stateful SGs/NAT gateway without restrictive stateless NACLs for those subnets.
- If they must deny ranges, use a narrower allowlist mapping and an egress proxy that keeps source ports predictable.
dustin-cust: We applied the allow for 32768-65535 on egress and corresponding inbound ephemeral allow, redeployed NAT, and streaming appears stable in our QA env. We'll roll to prod after security signoff. Any config snippet we can pass to infra team?
jamie-support: Here's a small Terraform-friendly patch to add to their `aws_network_acl_rule`:

```
resource "aws_network_acl_rule" "allow_ephemeral_egress" {
  network_acl_id = var.acl_id
  rule_number    = 65000
  egress         = true
  protocol       = "6"
  rule_action    = "allow"
  cidr_block     = "0.0.0.0/0"
  port_range { from = 32768 to = 65535 }
}

resource "aws_network_acl_rule" "allow_ephemeral_ingress" {
  network_acl_id = var.acl_id
  rule_number    = 65001
  egress         = false
  protocol       = "6"
  rule_action    = "allow"
  cidr_block     = "0.0.0.0/0"
  port_range { from = 32768 to = 65535 }
}
```

lina-sre: Note: pick rule numbers that place these allows before any wider deny entries. NACLs processed by rule number ascending; later rules can still match if earlier ones don't.
networking-jen: Also remind them that ALLOW on SGs is sufficient and simpler — SGs are stateful, so you only need to open 443 outbound on SG and return is automatically allowed. NACLs are useful for broad subnet-level controls but often cause subtle issues.
dustin-cust: Thanks. We'll pass this to infra and confirm. Appreciate the quick triage.
jamie-support: Closing for now — will reopen if they see recurrence after prod rollout. :thumbsup:
